A fashion brand sells on a large online fashion platform in twelve European countries. You have its sales by article type and country for two collections, Spring/Summer 2025 and 2026. The brand manager asks: **where do product page views turn into sales, and should we invest in Switzerland, our newest market?**

| Step | What | Time |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Coding exercise** in pairs: Tasks 1 to 5 below with the packages (polars, great_tables, statsmodels, plotnine) | 20 minutes |
| 2 | **Plenary**: the answers | 5 minutes |
| 3 | **Posit Assistant**: the same tasks with the assistant; compare its code, numbers and wording with yours (last section) | 10 minutes |

Use `regression_assumptions.qmd` as a template: log-log models, `C()` dummies, `exp(b) − 1` and the tests are the same.

## The data

`data/fashion/fashion_countries.csv` (see `data/fashion/README.md`): one row per season, country and article type, 403 rows. Real data, anonymised: volumes and money are rescaled, shares and conversion are original. This file sits in `sessions/01-foundations/`, so it reads the data two folders up.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `season`, `country`, `article_type` | SS25 or SS26; AT, BE, CH, CZ, DE, DK, FI, FR, IT, NL, PL, SE; Dress, Trouser, … |
| `pdp_views` | product page views |
| `sold_articles`, `conversion_pct` | articles sold; sold per 100 page views |
| `avg_item_value` | average gross price per sold article (incl. VAT) |
| `nmv` | net merchandise value: sales net of VAT |
| `discount_pct`, `size_availability_pct` | average discount; share of sizes in stock |
| `return_rate_pct` | estimated return rate, SS26 only |

fashion.head()
